steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition. Beat in vanilla.
Stir together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt in a separate bowl. Gradually add flour mixture to butter mixture and mix until blended.
Mix in oats and butterscotch chips until combined.
Drop dough by teaspoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet. Bake in the preheated oven until the edges begin to brown, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Butterscotch Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These butterscotch cookies are made with oats and loaded with sweet butterscotch chips for a crispy chewy cookie full of rich caramel flavor.

review.reviewBody: For those of you having trouble with the cookies being, dry, crumbly, or are having trouble removing them from the cookie sheet, it's probably because there is not enough butter in the dough. Try a full cup of butter, not 3/4 cup. For those having trouble with flat cookies, simply refrigerate your dough until it is somewhat firm.

These cookies are sooo yummy! I took some of the suggestions and lowered the temperature to 350 also and baked for about 9 minutes. I also refrigerated the dough for about 5 minutes and greased the cookie sheets with Pam. They turned out chewy and disappeared quickly! Thanks for the great recipe! :-)

The perfect cookie, in my mind, has a crisp outside and chewy center. This recipe (with some adjustments) is exactly that! I MADE THEM GLUTEN FREE with fantastic results! Here are the changes I made: I used gfJules all purpose flour (the best hands down!) in the same amount called for in this recipe. I added ½ cup butter flavored Crisco to the butter called for. I also used GF oats, cane sugar, and added the whole bag of butterscotch chips. The rest of the recipe was followed as written. I refrigerated the covered dough for 1+ hours. To bake, I used a 1 tablespoon cookie scoop on Silpat liners, and baked at 350 degrees (my convection oven automatically knocks that down to 325) for 11 minutes. You want to pull them out right as the edges start to hint at turning brown. They will look puffy and under-baked, but they will be perfect. Trust me. Leave them on that hot pan for 5 minutes (set your timer) and then move to a cooling rack. During the initial cool down on the pan, you will see them solidify and continue to darken ever so slightly. This recipe, with my changes, made 70 cookies. Once cooled, they are sturdy enough to pack up without breaking. I will store them in an airtight container on the counter. They are sweet, but not overly so. There is the slightest hint of cinnamon, it’s only a bit of an undertone, but it absolutely takes this cookie to the next level. I wouldn’t add more, but I wouldn’t leave it out.

These cookies are very good. I did take the advice of a few reviewers regarding the baking temperature,time,amount of sugar,butter, and flour. I also put them in the fridge for a while. I would say about 30 minutes as someone suggested. My cookies came out just right not too flat not too thick. The only ones that flattened a bit were the ones that had less dough and had more butterscotch morsels in it. This happended with my last batch. I highly recommend using 1/2 a cup of each of the sugars,because the butterscotch morsels will add the rest. Add the full cup of butter and 1 1/2 cup of flour. Bake for no more than 8 minutes and always do a test cookie according to the baking sheet you have. Darker sheets tend to brown them faster than the lighter colored ones. I also have a rule of letting the sheets cool off completely before putting more cookies on the same sheet. The principle is simple: a warm cookie sheet will start the melting of the butter much faster and therefore your cookie has a higher chance of spreading and burning. Please do refrigerate the dough before baking it this will also contribute to decrease the spreading. EDIT: I just made these cookies after a long time without baking them. I strongly suggest to lower the temperature to 350F and bake for 8 minutes only. This should be enough to prevent over baking of the cookie, spreading, and burning of the morsels.

This was my first time making this recipe, first time using oatmeal, and my first time ever using a stand mixer, and they turned out great! Crispy on the outside, soft on the inside. I followed the recipe mostly as written, but it seems the consensus is that more butter was required, so I took the advice of user auntcandie, and used 1 cup (2 sticks) of butter and increased the flour to 1 1/2 cups. Other users did a few other things, but that is all I changed. I also followed the recommendation to use Guittard butterscotch chips. I ordered 3 bags directly from their website to get free shipping and to make sure I had enough in case of a mishap, and I ended up using one full bag. I used a #24 cookie scoop, and it made pretty large cookies, but that’s what I wanted, and it yielded 26 cookies. I initially put them in the oven for 8 minutes, but they ended up going about 12 minutes. Since I wasn’t entirely sure what I was looking for, I probably could have taken them out a minute sooner, but they still turned out great. My husband gave them two thumbs up. I will definitely make these again.
They stuck to the pan terribly. I chilled the dough, used parchment paper, and lowered the temp to 350. The remaining cookies were much better.

I made this recipe on 6/20/20 in a muffin tin & they were a big hit! I followed the recipe & will make it again. The muffin tin gives the cookies a slight crisp on the bottom & sides while the center & top remain chewy; it's an excellent combination of textures. YUMMY!

Definitely recommend!

Outstanding cookies! I have been baking for many (MANY!) decades. I have been looking for a 'chip' recipe that uses butter. I almost always put oatmeal in my cookies, and usually use semi-sweet and butterscotch chips combined. 

I tried these with just a couple of tweaks based on comments. I used 1 c. (2 sticks) of butter, and increased the flour to 1 1/2 c. Cookies came off the sheet perfectly (let cool 6 minutes before removing to rack) and held their shape perfectly. 

They are moist and chewy and perfect. I left them out, uncovered on counter to see how they were on day #2 and they had not changed at all. Hurray!!

I recommend Guittard's Butterscotch chips for incredible flavor. Head and shoulders above Nestle's and store brands. Made 3 dozen nice-sized cookies using my medium scoop. Neighbors and SIL raved.

I increased the butter to 1 cup and reduced the white sugar to 1 1/8 cups and the taste was great. Those butterscotch chips are sweet so I can see reducing the white sugar even more. I also chilled before baking which made the dough easier to work with and the cookies stayed a bit thicker, which I like. Using ping-pong ball size, I baked at 350 for 12 minutes. Be aware that if you do not chill the dough, this may be too long to bake.

We love these cookies; however, I did make some changes. I decreased the oats to 2 3/4 cups and increased the flour to 1 1/2 cups. I cooked them at 300 degrees for 15 minutes and turned the cookie sheet around halfway through. This lower temperature made it so that they did not spread too much and over cook the edges. They came out perfect!

After reading reviews, I increased the butter to a full cup and refrigerated the scooped cookies before baking. I used an 1.5oz scoop, and it made 30 cookies. I also increased the cinnamon to a full tsp. And they are perfect.
Perfect cookies I added 3/4 c slightly chopped pecans.
We added chocolate chunks & coconut shreds. This is my kids new favorite cookie!
Add baking powder or they will be flat
Yes I baked these oatmeal 🥣 butter scotchie cookies! But I kept in oven for 20 minutes at 375 degrees instead of 10 minutes! And they are delicious golden brown🧡🧡🧡 Thank you

Tasted good, but looked terrible!!! I used a good quality baking sheet, chilled dough for an hour invthe fridge, spaced them properly and they were super flat, almost like a lace cookie, and they ran together. Will never make again. Very frustrating....
Great cookie! I baked at 350* for 10 minutes. It made about 3 & 1/2 dozen. Will bake again.
No changes. Good cookie

I made these for one of my husband's get togethers. The flavor was top notch. I did add a touch more butter as one of the other commenters suggested but I am sure they would have been fine without it, too.
I refrigerated the dough for 24 hrs made them soft and chewy
